summary: Both numbers are right for their own definition. The dashboard reports what Sales sold in Q1; the ledger reports what Finance recognised in Q1. Four rules differ, and together they explain the {{gap_q1_2026|money0}} exactly. The fix is not to change the Sales number silently but to add the ledger definition as its own measure, label both, and use Net Revenue (Ledger) wherever the dashboard is compared with the board pack.
root_cause: Staff purchases ({{staff_q1_2026|money0}} net) are revenue on the dashboard but cost recovery in the ledger (policy 4.2).

Sales date: the dashboard uses the order date; the ledger uses the posting date. Orders placed after 18:00 on the last day of a month post the next day. {{posting_orders_out|int}} order(s) from 31 March ({{posting_out_of_q1|money0}}) are April revenue for Finance, and {{posting_orders_in|int}} order(s) from 31 December ({{posting_into_q1|money0}}) are Q1 revenue for Finance.

Returns timing: the dashboard deducts refunds from the period of the original order (including {{returns_april_for_q1|money0}} refunded in April for Q1 orders); the ledger deducts them when the goods come back (policy 4.3), including {{returns_q1_for_prior|money0}} received in Q1 for orders from 2025.
Shipping refunds ({{fin_ship_q1_2026|money0}}) reduce revenue in the ledger (policy 4.4); the dashboard ignores the ShippingRefund column.
steps: Don't argue about which number is right. Reproduce both numbers from the same data first: if you can rebuild the ledger from the order data, the difference is definitional, not a data error.
Reconcile by month, not by quarter. Nina is right that every month differs by a different amount, which already rules out a single cause.
Read the policy as a specification. Items 4.1 to 4.4 and 4.7 apply to this data; 4.5 (gift cards) and 4.6 (intercompany) are distractors with no rows in the extract.

Bridge one rule at a time from the dashboard to the ledger and keep a running total. Here the order is: remove Staff, switch sales to posting date (and its month's FX rate), switch returns to return date, deduct shipping refunds.
When the bridge lands on the ledger to the dollar, stop investigating. You've explained the gap; anything else would be a new problem.

Model both definitions: keep Net Sales (order date) for the Sales view; add Net Revenue (Ledger) using an inactive relationship on PostingDate (USERELATIONSHIP), returns by ReturnDate, excluding Staff, minus shipping refunds.
Regression check: Gross Sales, Net Sales and YoY from Sprint 01 must still show the same values after the change.
Reply to Sarah with the gap, the four causes and the proposed labelling, and copy Jordan. Offer a ten-minute call; don't send a spreadsheet without a sentence on top.

artifacts.title: DAX: the ledger definition, next to the Sales one
body: -- FactSales has an inactive relationship FactSales[PostingDate] → DimDate[Date]
-- FactReturns relates to DimDate on ReturnDate (active) and to the original order line
Ledger Sales =
CALCULATE (
SUM ( FactSales[GrossUSDAtPosting] ),         -- EUR translated at the posting month's rate
USERELATIONSHIP ( FactSales[PostingDate], DimDate[Date] ),
KEEPFILTERS ( DimChannel[Channel] <> "Staff" )
Ledger Returns =
CALCULATE (
SUM ( FactReturns[RefundUSDAtReturn] ) + SUM ( FactReturns[ShippingRefundUSDAtReturn] ),
KEEPFILTERS ( DimChannel[Channel] <> "Staff" )
Net Revenue (Ledger) = [Ledger Sales] - [Ledger Returns]
Sales vs Ledger Gap = [Net Sales] - [Net Revenue (Ledger)]   -- keep it visible on a reconciliation page

artifacts.title: Reply to the CFO
body: **Subject: Q1 net revenue: dashboard vs ledger, explained**
Sarah, the {{gap_q1_2026|money0}} difference is fully explained by four definition differences, not by errors in either number:
- Staff purchases ({{staff_q1_2026|money0}}): revenue for Sales, cost recovery in the ledger.
- Month-end cut-off: the dashboard uses order date, the ledger posting date ({{bridge_posting|smoney0}} net).
- Returns: the dashboard deducts them from the original sale's period, the ledger when goods come back ({{bridge_returns|smoney0}}).
- Shipping refunds: deducted in the ledger, not on the dashboard ({{bridge_shipping|smoney0}}).

Proposal: the dashboard keeps Sales' view, labelled "Net Sales (orders)", and adds "Net Revenue (ledger)", which matches the GL to the dollar. Anything compared with the board pack uses the ledger measure. Jordan is copied; happy to take ten minutes today.

communication.executive: Neither number is wrong. Sales counts what was ordered in Q1; Finance counts what was booked in Q1. Four accounting rules make the difference. The dashboard will show both, clearly labelled, and the board will see Finance's.
communication.engineer: Bridge from Net Sales to the ledger: −Staff ({{bridge_staff|smoney0}}), order→posting date with posting-month FX ({{bridge_posting|smoney0}}), refunds by return date ({{bridge_returns|smoney0}}), shipping refunds ({{bridge_shipping|smoney0}}). Implemented as Net Revenue (Ledger) with USERELATIONSHIP on PostingDate; Sprint 01 measures unchanged (regression check attached).

pitfalls: Changing the existing Net Sales measure to match Finance. Every Sales report that used it changes overnight, and Jordan's Q1 slide is now wrong.
Explaining 90% of the gap and calling the rest "rounding". The board pack needs it to the dollar; small residuals often hide a fifth cause.
Taking sides. Both teams follow a consistent rule; the problem is one word ("revenue") meaning two things.
Using the order month's FX rate for posted sales: the ledger translates at the posting month's rate (4.7).

review.junior: Assumes the dashboard is wrong, changes the measure until it matches the ledger total for the quarter, and doesn't notice the months still differ.
review.competent: Builds a monthly comparison, finds the posting date and returns timing, and adds a second measure.
review.senior: Rebuilds the ledger from source to prove the gap is definitional, bridges all four causes to the cent, keeps both definitions with unambiguous names, regression-tests Sprint 01, and writes one calm email to both stakeholders.
review.architect: Sees that "revenue" needs an owner and one certified definition per purpose. Proposes a KPI dictionary owned by Finance, a certified semantic model that carries both measures, and a rule that dashboards compared with the board pack use the ledger measure. That is Sprint 05.
